decisions.reason: The current thm-qftx-wavefront-product Proof 3.1 explicitly derives the absolutely convergent localized Fourier convolution and identifies it with diagonal pullback. Thus F3 is supported by the actual supplier argument, even though the displayed Statement only gives the product and wavefront bound. The assigned lemma itself proves uniform polynomial bounds (1.1–2.1), uniform regular-cone decay (3.1), and the two-region integrable majorant (4.1); joint center transversality and nonnegative bounds are retained. No missing Fourier premise or item edit is justified by this tuple.

The adjective analytic had no parameter or analyticity definition. This is a confirmed terminology defect: the preceding scaling clause already requires preservation of the actual scaling degree, not an additional holomorphic regularization. The repair specifies the exact relative distribution, dimension, finite-real degree and family E_delta(t), with the degree-minus-infinity uniqueness case, and defines analytic extension stage as the distribution-theoretic step. It retains all actual-degree and engineering-bound requirements and distinguishes these from the parameter-dependent analytic regularizations in FR equations (93)–(97).

The original step 4.1 applies a theorem about support at a single point directly to a distribution supported on the entire total diagonal. This misses an essential hypothesis at the cited use. Repaired steps 4.1 and 5.1 prove the center/relative decomposition Q=1_y tensor q from translation invariance, using compact primitives of tests with zero center integral, then classify the point-supported relative distribution q. The resulting integrated delta-jet formula proves finite local polynomial output, support inclusion and covariance coefficientwise. The Statement also explicitly types the formal C[[hbar]] modules and interaction-degree completion, resolving the digest concern without weakening the claim.

A1 expressly attributes the assumptions to the anomaly proposition’s suppliers. In that current published proposition, F7 cites the polar-coordinate formula under Countable Choice, F6 states AC implies Countable Choice, and A1 supplies it to F4/F7 from AC. Thus the example does not assert a stronger independent hypothesis of the anomaly proposition; its separately declared AC and Countable Choice are sufficient and redundant. The cutoff-integral subtraction gives the positive (8 pi^2)^(-1) logarithmic coefficient; dimension four permits only a scalar delta ambiguity. The two-vertex TikZ has exactly two parallel internal lines and two external slots at each vertex, as stated.
